one_liner: Senior data and process-improvement analyst for the Capitol's safety office: tracks safety metrics and KPIs, runs Six Sigma projects, briefs executives, and oversees contractors as a COR.
fit_summary: This GS-13 analytics role requires 52 weeks of GS-12-level statistical, trend, root-cause and predictive analysis, plus Six Sigma and COR work. Daniel has a Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt and Excel pivot-table reporting, but not senior-level quantitative analytics, so he likely won't qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring path: public), and U.S. citizens are eligible, so no federal status is needed.

GS-13 requires at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12. That means professional use of statistical, comparative, trend, diagnostic, root cause and predictive methods to analyze organizational and mission performance.
You must meet the OPM qualification standards by the closing date of November 16, 2026.
No security clearance is required, and the role is telework-eligible but not remote (Washington, DC).
strategy: His analysis work (Excel pivot-table reports, FEMA onboarding data, exercise notes used for after-action reports) is real but not a year of GS-12-level statistical analysis, so skip this unless he has more.

Frame IEM experience in posting language. For example, 'analyzed disaster recovery program performance data to identify trends and root causes for government clients,' stated only where true, with hours per week and dates.

Within the two-page limit, put specialized experience first. Name the tools you used (Excel, Power BI, Tableau, SQL, statistics) and any Six Sigma or Lean training, and briefly note briefings delivered to government senior leaders.

Preview the self-assessment questions on Data Analytics, Oral Communication and Written Communication. Answer 'expert' only where a resume bullet proves it, because inflated answers that the resume doesn't support get screened out.
Apply between Oct 28 and Nov 16, 2026, and submit well before midnight Eastern on the closing day. Check the announcement for any required documents, such as transcripts if you claim education.
If you don't qualify, consider lower-grade analyst roles (GS-9/11) or communications and legislative-affairs roles that better match your policy and people strengths.
resume_bullets: Completed Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt training.
Built Excel pivot-table reports on spending and order status (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Describe a time you used trend or root-cause analysis to identify a problem and recommend a fix. What data and methods did you use?
How would you design KPIs to measure the effectiveness of a workplace safety program?
Tell us about translating complex data findings for a senior leader or non-technical audience.
Have you overseen contractor deliverables or served in a COR-type role? How did you handle disputes over performance?
watch_outs: This is high-grade technical analytics work, so without documented statistical or predictive analysis experience you are unlikely to pass qualification screening.
The duties include COR responsibilities and OSHA compliance knowledge; COR certification may be expected or required after hire.
The commute from Manassas to Capitol Hill is long, though telework eligibility may help.
